entries.meaning: To come to believe that something is true, or to agree to take what is offered. ---
examples: I accept that we may never know the whole story.
She accepted the job offer on Friday.
They have accepted our explanation without argument.

entries.meaning: Acknowledge has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Both sides acknowledge that the talks have stalled.
He acknowledged his mistake in front of the whole team.
The company has never acknowledged the problem.
Please acknowledge receipt of this email.
They never acknowledged my application.
The office has acknowledged our letter but has not answered it.

senses.head: To admit that something is true or that someone deserves attention
examples: Both sides acknowledge that the talks have stalled.
He acknowledged his mistake in front of the whole team.
The company has never acknowledged the problem.

senses.head: To tell someone that you have received what they sent
examples: Please acknowledge receipt of this email.
They never acknowledged my application.
The office has acknowledged our letter but has not answered it.

entries.meaning: To examine something in detail in order to understand how it works. ---
examples: Let us analyze the numbers before we decide.
The lab analyzed the water samples overnight.
She is analyzing the survey results right now.
entries.contrast: American analyze; British analyse.

entries.meaning: To expect something and get ready for it. ---
examples: Good drivers anticipate what other cars will do.
Nobody anticipated such a long delay.
We are anticipating a busy weekend.

entries.meaning: To judge the quality, size, or value of something. ---
examples: Teachers assess each student twice a year.
The inspector assessed the damage in an hour.
The risk has not been properly assessed.

entries.meaning: Assume has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Do not assume that everyone has read the email.
I assumed you were coming with us.
We had assumed the store was open on Sundays.
She assumed command of the unit in March.
The buyer will assume the rest of the debt.
He has assumed full responsibility for the mistake.
He assumed an air of total innocence.
The spy had assumed a new identity before crossing the border.
Actors often assume an accent for a role.

senses.head: To accept that something is true without proof
examples: Do not assume that everyone has read the email.
I assumed you were coming with us.
We had assumed the store was open on Sundays.

senses.head: To take on a duty, a position of power, or a responsibility
body: (принимать на себя, взять на себя (обязанности); вступать в должность)
examples: She assumed command of the unit in March.
The buyer will assume the rest of the debt.
He has assumed full responsibility for the mistake.

senses.head: To put on a manner, an appearance, or a name that is not really your own
examples: He assumed an air of total innocence.
The spy had assumed a new identity before crossing the border.
Actors often assume an accent for a role.

entries.русский: предполагать, полагать; принимать на себя, взять на себя (обязанности); вступать в должность; принимать (вид), напускать на себя; присваивать (чужое имя)

entries.meaning: To think that something is true or that someone is telling the truth. ---
examples: I believe she is telling the truth.
Nobody believed his story at first.
He has always believed in working hard.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (I believe you), intransitive (seeing is believing)
entries.contrast: believe someone = верить кому-то; believe in someone = верить в кого-то.

entries.meaning: To think up as many ideas as possible, usually with other people. ---
examples: Let us brainstorm a few titles for the article.
We brainstormed for an hour and filled two whiteboards.
They are brainstorming names for the new product.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (brainstorm ideas), intransitive (let us brainstorm)

entries.meaning: To work something out using numbers. ---
examples: The app calculates the tip for you.
I calculated the cost per person.
Shipping has already been calculated.

entries.meaning: Classify has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Libraries classify books by subject.
The doctor classified the case as mild.
These documents are classified as secret.
The agency can classify anything it calls sensitive.
The Pentagon classified the report for thirty years.
Most of the file is still classified.

senses.head: To put people or things into groups by type
examples: Libraries classify books by subject.
The doctor classified the case as mild.
These documents are classified as secret.

senses.head: To declare officially that information is secret
examples: The agency can classify anything it calls sensitive.
The Pentagon classified the report for thirty years.
Most of the file is still classified.

entries.русский: классифицировать, относить к категории; засекречивать, засекретить
entries.contrast: The -y turns into -ies and -ied: classifies, classified.

entries.meaning: To look at two or more things in order to see how they are alike or different. ---
examples: Compare the two offers before you sign anything.
We compared prices at three stores.
This car is often compared to a small SUV.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (compare prices), intransitive (how do the two compare?)
entries.contrast: compare to points out a likeness; compare with weighs two things side by side.

entries.meaning: To understand something fully, especially something difficult; a formal word where speech would use understand. ---
examples: Few people comprehend how large that number really is.
She comprehended the danger at once.
He sat there, not comprehending a word.

entries.meaning: Conceive has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I cannot conceive of a simpler solution.
She conceived the whole project on a train ride.
The bridge was conceived in the 1930s.
Many couples conceive within a year of trying.
She conceived shortly after the treatment.
The twins were conceived through IVF.

senses.head: To form an idea or a plan in your mind
examples: I cannot conceive of a simpler solution.
She conceived the whole project on a train ride.
The bridge was conceived in the 1930s.

senses.head: To become pregnant
examples: Many couples conceive within a year of trying.
She conceived shortly after the treatment.
The twins were conceived through IVF.

entries.transitivity: both — transitive (conceive a plan), intransitive (conceive of a world without money)
entries.contrast: After c the spelling is -ei-: conceive, receive, perceive.

entries.meaning: Concede has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I concede that the price is fair.
The candidate conceded on election night.
Having conceded the point, he changed the subject.
He refused to concede until every vote was counted.
She conceded on Wednesday morning.
Neither candidate has conceded yet.

senses.head: To admit that something is true, often unwillingly
examples: I concede that the price is fair.
The candidate conceded on election night.
Having conceded the point, he changed the subject.

senses.head: To admit publicly that you have lost an election or a contest
examples: He refused to concede until every vote was counted.
She conceded on Wednesday morning.
Neither candidate has conceded yet.

entries.русский: признавать, уступать; признавать поражение, признать поражение
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (concede a point), intransitive (he conceded at last)

entries.meaning: Concentrate has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I cannot concentrate with the TV on.
She concentrated on the hardest questions first.
He was concentrating so hard that he did not hear me.
Most of the new jobs concentrate in two counties.
The company concentrated its factories in the South.
Wealth has become concentrated in a handful of cities.

senses.head: To give all your attention to one thing
examples: I cannot concentrate with the TV on.
She concentrated on the hardest questions first.
He was concentrating so hard that he did not hear me.

senses.head: To gather in one place in large amounts, or to bring things together in one place
examples: Most of the new jobs concentrate in two counties.
The company concentrated its factories in the South.
Wealth has become concentrated in a handful of cities.

entries.русский: сосредотачиваться, сосредоточиться; сосредотачивать, сосредоточить; скапливаться, концентрировать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (concentrate your efforts), intransitive (I cannot concentrate)
entries.contrast: You concentrate on something, never concentrate at something.

entries.meaning: Conclude has 3 distinct senses.
examples: What do you conclude from these numbers?
The jury concluded that he was innocent.
Researchers have concluded that the drug is safe.
We usually conclude the meeting with questions.
The concert concluded with an encore.
The trial has concluded after six weeks.
The two countries hope to conclude a trade deal this year.
They concluded an agreement in March.
A cease-fire was concluded on Friday.

senses.head: To decide that something is true after thinking about the facts
examples: What do you conclude from these numbers?
The jury concluded that he was innocent.
Researchers have concluded that the drug is safe.

senses.head: To bring something to an end, or to come to an end
examples: We usually conclude the meeting with questions.
The concert concluded with an encore.
The trial has concluded after six weeks.

senses.head: To formally arrange and finish an agreement
examples: The two countries hope to conclude a trade deal this year.
They concluded an agreement in March.
A cease-fire was concluded on Friday.

entries.русский: заключать, делать вывод; завершать, завершить; заканчиваться, закончиться; заключать, заключить (договор, соглашение)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (conclude the meeting), intransitive (the study concluded)

entries.meaning: To mix one thing up with another, or to make someone unable to think clearly. ---
examples: People often confuse the two brothers.
The map only confused us more.
I am always confusing their names.
entries.contrast: You confuse one thing with another.

entries.meaning: To think carefully about something before deciding, or to hold an opinion about it. ---
examples: We consider him the best teacher in the school.
They considered three cities before choosing Denver.
She is considering moving back home.
entries.contrast: consider doing something, never consider to do something.

entries.meaning: To think about something long and seriously. ---
examples: He likes to contemplate such questions on long walks.
She contemplated quitting, then stayed another year.
They are contemplating a move to Texas.
entries.contrast: contemplate doing something, not contemplate to do something.

entries.meaning: Decide has 2 distinct senses.
examples: You decide where we eat tonight.
We decided to take the early flight.
Nothing has been decided yet.
One goal can decide a game like this.
A single vote decided the election.
The title was decided in overtime.

senses.head: To make a choice after thinking about it
examples: You decide where we eat tonight.
We decided to take the early flight.
Nothing has been decided yet.

senses.head: To settle the result of a game, a contest, or a question
examples: One goal can decide a game like this.
A single vote decided the election.
The title was decided in overtime.

entries.русский: решать, решить; решать исход, определять; предрешать
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (decide the winner), intransitive (you decide)
entries.contrast: decide to do something; decide on a thing.

entries.meaning: To work something out from the facts you already have. ---
examples: From the ashes you can deduce what burned.
She deduced his age from his school photos.
Little can be deduced from a single bad test.

entries.meaning: To consider something to be a certain way, in formal or official language. ---
examples: The court may deem the contract invalid.
Officials deemed the building unsafe.
The proposal was deemed too expensive.

entries.meaning: To show clearly that something is true, or to show how something works. ---
examples: These numbers demonstrate the problem better than words do.
He demonstrated the machine for us.
The study has demonstrated a clear link.

entries.meaning: To notice something that is hard to see, hear, or measure. ---
examples: Dogs can detect smells we cannot.
I detected a note of doubt in her voice.
No errors were detected in the code.

entries.meaning: To find out something for certain, or to settle it. ---
examples: Tests will determine the cause.
The judge determined that the search was legal.
The route has not been determined yet.

entries.meaning: To invent a plan, a system, or a method. ---
examples: We need to devise a fairer schedule.
He devised a way to cut the wait in half.
They are devising a new grading system.
entries.contrast: The verb devise ends in a /z/ sound; the noun device ends in /s/.

entries.meaning: To find out about something for the first time. ---
examples: Kids discover something new every day.
We discovered the leak too late.
A second entrance has been discovered.

entries.meaning: Dismiss has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Do not dismiss the idea so quickly.
He dismissed my worries with a laugh.
The complaint was dismissed by the court.
The school dismissed two teachers after the investigation.
An employer cannot dismiss you for taking sick leave.
He is suing the company for dismissing him without warning.
The teacher dismisses the class at three o'clock.
The principal dismissed the students early because of the storm.
We were dismissed as soon as the drill ended.

senses.head: To decide that an idea or a person is not worth taking seriously
examples: Do not dismiss the idea so quickly.
He dismissed my worries with a laugh.
The complaint was dismissed by the court.

senses.head: To officially remove someone from a job
examples: The school dismissed two teachers after the investigation.
An employer cannot dismiss you for taking sick leave.
He is suing the company for dismissing him without warning.

senses.head: To tell a group of people that they may leave
examples: The teacher dismisses the class at three o'clock.
The principal dismissed the students early because of the storm.
We were dismissed as soon as the drill ended.

entries.русский: отвергать, отмахиваться; увольнять, уволить; отпускать, распускать (класс, собрание)

entries.meaning: Distinguish has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Can you distinguish the twins?
She distinguished the real bills from the fakes.
Young children have trouble distinguishing between fact and fantasy.
In the fog we could barely distinguish the shoreline.
She distinguished three figures moving along the ridge.
Even with binoculars he had trouble distinguishing the bird against the rocks.
Cadets who distinguish themselves are offered command posts.
She distinguished herself as a trial lawyer before turning forty.
He has distinguished himself in three different fields.

senses.head: To see or explain the difference between things
examples: Can you distinguish the twins?
She distinguished the real bills from the fakes.
Young children have trouble distinguishing between fact and fantasy.

senses.head: To manage to see or hear something that is hard to make out
examples: In the fog we could barely distinguish the shoreline.
She distinguished three figures moving along the ridge.
Even with binoculars he had trouble distinguishing the bird against the rocks.

senses.head: To do something so well that people notice and admire you
examples: Cadets who distinguish themselves are offered command posts.
She distinguished herself as a trial lawyer before turning forty.
He has distinguished himself in three different fields.

entries.русский: различать, отличать; разглядеть, различить (с трудом); отличиться, проявить себя
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (distinguish the twins), intransitive (distinguish between them)
entries.contrast: distinguish between two things, or distinguish one from another.

entries.meaning: To think that something is probably not true or will probably not happen. ---
examples: I doubt he will call back.
Nobody doubted her honesty.
He has never doubted his own judgment.
entries.contrast: The b is silent: DOWT. The same silent b appears in debt and subtle.

entries.meaning: To picture in your mind how something could be in the future. ---
examples: I envision a small shop with two or three tables.
The founders envisioned a free library in every town.
The park is envisioned as a green corridor.

entries.meaning: To make a rough judgment about an amount, a size, or a cost. ---
examples: Can you estimate how long the drive takes?
The contractor estimated six weeks of work.
Damage is estimated at two million dollars.
entries.contrast: The verb is ES-tuh-mayt; the noun estimate ends in a schwa: ES-tuh-muht.

entries.meaning: To judge carefully how good or how useful something is. ---
examples: We evaluate every applicant the same way.
The team evaluated four suppliers.
The program is being evaluated this fall.

entries.meaning: To look at something closely in order to learn about it. ---
examples: Let us examine the contract line by line.
The doctor examined her knee.
The evidence has been examined by two experts.

entries.meaning: Expect has 2 distinct senses.
examples: We expect about thirty guests.
I expected the test to be harder.
Rain is expected by evening.
The school expects students to be in their seats by eight.
You are expected to answer emails within a day.
We expected better manners from a grown man.

senses.head: To believe that something will happen or that someone will do something
examples: We expect about thirty guests.
I expected the test to be harder.
Rain is expected by evening.

senses.head: To require something of someone because you consider it their duty
examples: The school expects students to be in their seats by eight.
You are expected to answer emails within a day.
We expected better manners from a grown man.

entries.русский: ожидать, рассчитывать; требовать, ожидать (чего-л. от кого-л.)
entries.contrast: expect someone to do something: I expect you to be on time.

entries.meaning: To be afraid of something, or to believe with worry that it is true. ---
examples: Many parents fear that the school will close.
We feared the worst when the phone rang at three in the morning.
Twelve people are feared missing.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (fear the worst), intransitive (never fear)

entries.meaning: Focus has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Let us focus on the first chapter.
He focused on his breathing and calmed down.
She is focusing on her health this year.
Let me focus the camera before you move.
He focused the binoculars on the far shore.
Her eyes wouldn't focus after the drops.

senses.head: To give your attention to one thing rather than to many
examples: Let us focus on the first chapter.
He focused on his breathing and calmed down.
She is focusing on her health this year.

senses.head: To adjust a camera or your eyes so that what you see is sharp
examples: Let me focus the camera before you move.
He focused the binoculars on the far shore.
Her eyes wouldn't focus after the drops.

entries.русский: сосредотачиваться, фокусироваться; наводить резкость, фокусировать, сфокусировать; фокусироваться (о зрении)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (focus the camera), intransitive (focus on the task)
entries.contrast: American English keeps one s: focused, focusing. You focus on something.

entries.meaning: To understand an idea, especially a difficult one. ---
examples: It took me a while to grasp what she meant.
He never really grasped the math behind it.
The rule is easily grasped once you see an example.

entries.meaning: To give an answer you are not sure of, or to suppose something. ---
examples: I guess we should leave now.
You guessed the number on the first try.
I was only guessing, and I got lucky.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (guess the answer), intransitive (go ahead and guess)
entries.contrast: The third person adds -es: guesses.

entries.meaning: To pause before doing something because you are unsure. ---
examples: Do not hesitate to call if you need help.
She hesitated for a second, then signed.
He is still hesitating over the price.
entries.contrast: hesitate to do something.

entries.meaning: To want something to happen and believe that it might. ---
examples: We hope to see you in June.
I hoped the rain would stop.
She is hoping for a scholarship.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (I hope so), intransitive (we can only hope)
entries.contrast: Drop the e: hoping, not hopeing. You hope for a thing and hope to do something.

entries.meaning: To recognize who or what someone or something is. ---
examples: Can you identify the plant from this photo?
Witnesses identified the car right away.
The victims have not been identified.
entries.contrast: The -y turns into -ies and -ied: identifies, identified.

entries.meaning: To pay no attention to someone or something on purpose. ---
examples: Just ignore the noise from upstairs.
He ignored three warning emails.
The advice was ignored completely.

entries.meaning: Imagine has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Imagine a city with no cars.
I imagined the room much bigger.
She is imagining problems that do not exist.
I imagine they'll cancel the flight.
Everyone imagined the deal was already done.
I had imagined the drive would take about an hour.

senses.head: To form a picture of something in your mind
examples: Imagine a city with no cars.
I imagined the room much bigger.
She is imagining problems that do not exist.

senses.head: To think that something is probably true; to suppose
examples: I imagine they'll cancel the flight.
Everyone imagined the deal was already done.
I had imagined the drive would take about an hour.

entries.русский: воображать, представлять себе; полагать, предполагать; думать
entries.contrast: imagine doing something, not imagine to do something.

entries.meaning: Indicate has 2 distinct senses.
examples: These symptoms indicate a mild infection.
The survey indicated strong support.
Nothing has indicated a problem so far.
Sources indicate that the deal is close.
The mayor indicated she would run again.
Officials have indicated that no decision has been made.

senses.head: To show that something is true or likely
examples: These symptoms indicate a mild infection.
The survey indicated strong support.
Nothing has indicated a problem so far.

senses.head: To say something briefly or indirectly rather than stating it outright
examples: Sources indicate that the deal is close.
The mayor indicated she would run again.
Officials have indicated that no decision has been made.

entries.русский: указывать, свидетельствовать; давать понять, дать понять; сообщать, заявлять

entries.meaning: To reach a conclusion from evidence rather than from a direct statement. ---
examples: What do you infer from her silence?
The reader inferred that the narrator had died.
We are inferring a lot from very little data.
entries.contrast: The stress falls on the last syllable, so the r doubles: inferred, inferring.

entries.meaning: To plan to do something. ---
examples: We intend to stay two nights.
I never intended to hurt anyone.
The room was intended as a nursery.
entries.contrast: intend to do something.

entries.meaning: To decide what something means, or to put speech into another language. ---
examples: Courts interpret the law, they do not write it.
She interpreted his silence as anger.
He is interpreting for the visiting team.
entries.contrast: The t does not double, because the stress is not on the last syllable: interpreted.

entries.meaning: To think up something that did not exist before, including a false story. ---
examples: Kids invent games out of nothing.
He invented an excuse on the spot.
The zipper was invented over a century ago.

entries.meaning: To try to find out the truth about something by examining it. ---
examples: Reporters investigate stories like this for months.
The city investigated the complaint and found nothing.
Two agencies are investigating the crash.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (investigate a crime), intransitive (police are investigating)

entries.meaning: Judge has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Do not judge a book by its cover.
She judged the distance perfectly.
Judging by the sky, it will rain before noon.
Don't judge me — you weren't there.
She felt judged the moment she walked in.
People were judging him for something he said years ago.

senses.head: To form an opinion about someone or something after thinking about it
examples: Do not judge a book by its cover.
She judged the distance perfectly.
Judging by the sky, it will rain before noon.

senses.head: To criticize someone's choices or morals, usually unfairly
examples: Don't judge me — you weren't there.
She felt judged the moment she walked in.
People were judging him for something he said years ago.

entries.русский: судить, оценивать; осуждать, осудить; судить (о человеке)
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (judge a contest), intransitive (judging by his face)
entries.contrast: Drop the e: judging, not judgeing.

entries.meaning: To show that something is right or reasonable. ---
examples: Nothing can justify lying to them.
He justified the cost by pointing to the savings.
Her anger was completely justified.
entries.contrast: The -y turns into -ies and -ied: justifies, justified.

entries.meaning: To learn something so well that you can repeat it from memory. ---
examples: You do not need to memorize the formula.
He memorized the whole speech in two days.
She is memorizing her lines for the play.
entries.contrast: American memorize; British memorise.

entries.meaning: To see, hear, or become aware of something. ---
examples: Did you notice anything strange?
I noticed that the light was still on.
Nobody had noticed the mistake until then.
entries.contrast: Drop the e: noticing, not noticeing.

entries.meaning: Observe has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Student teachers observe a classroom before they teach in one.
He observed that nobody had touched the food.
The birds are being observed from a hide.
Drivers must observe the speed limit in a school zone.
Her family observed Passover at her grandmother's house.
A minute of silence was observed before the game.

senses.head: To watch something carefully, or to remark on what you see
examples: Student teachers observe a classroom before they teach in one.
He observed that nobody had touched the food.
The birds are being observed from a hide.

senses.head: To obey a law or rule, or to keep a holiday or custom
examples: Drivers must observe the speed limit in a school zone.
Her family observed Passover at her grandmother's house.
A minute of silence was observed before the game.

entries.meaning: Overlook has 2 distinct senses.
examples: It is easy to overlook a typo in your own writing.
The auditors overlooked two payments.
Her best work has been overlooked for years.
Our room overlooks the harbor.
The cabin overlooked a small lake.
We ate on a terrace overlooking the river.

senses.head: To fail to notice something, or to decide to let a fault pass
examples: It is easy to overlook a typo in your own writing.
The auditors overlooked two payments.
Her best work has been overlooked for years.

senses.head: To have a view over something from above
body: (выходить на (о виде из окна), возвышаться над)
examples: Our room overlooks the harbor.
The cabin overlooked a small lake.
We ate on a terrace overlooking the river.

entries.русский: упускать из виду, не замечать; выходить на (о виде из окна), возвышаться над
entries.contrast: One word, not a phrasal verb: you overlook a detail, but you look over a document to check it.

entries.meaning: To notice something with the senses, or to understand it in a certain way. ---
examples: Dogs perceive sounds we cannot hear.
She perceived at once that something was wrong.
The delay was perceived as an insult.
entries.contrast: After c the spelling is -ei-: perceive, receive, deceive.

entries.meaning: Picture has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Picture a beach with nobody on it.
I pictured the house as much older.
She is picturing herself on stage.
The magazine pictured her on the cover.
He is pictured here with his two daughters.
The mural pictures the town as it looked in 1900.

senses.head: To form an image of something in your mind
examples: Picture a beach with nobody on it.
I pictured the house as much older.
She is picturing herself on stage.

senses.head: To show someone or something in a photograph, a painting, or a film
examples: The magazine pictured her on the cover.
He is pictured here with his two daughters.
The mural pictures the town as it looked in 1900.

entries.русский: представлять себе, воображать; изображать, изобразить; снимать, снять (на фото)
entries.contrast: picture someone doing something: I can picture him teaching.

entries.meaning: To decide in advance how something will be done. ---
examples: We plan to leave at six.
They planned the wedding in three months.
She is planning a trip to Alaska.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (plan a trip), intransitive (plan ahead)
entries.contrast: One vowel plus one consonant, so the n doubles: planned, planning.

entries.meaning: To think about something slowly and seriously. ---
examples: He likes to ponder such questions on long walks.
She pondered the offer for a week.
They sat pondering what to do next.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (ponder the question), intransitive (ponder over a problem)

entries.meaning: To like one thing more than another. ---
examples: I prefer tea to coffee.
She preferred the second draft.
He has always preferred working at night.
entries.contrast: The r doubles in preferred and preferring, but not in the noun preference.

entries.meaning: Presume has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I presume you have already eaten.
The police presumed the car was stolen.
He is presumed innocent until proven guilty.
I wouldn't presume to tell you how to run your own shop.
She presumed to speak for the whole department.
No one has ever presumed to question his figures.

senses.head: To suppose that something is true because it is likely
examples: I presume you have already eaten.
The police presumed the car was stolen.
He is presumed innocent until proven guilty.

senses.head: To dare to do something you have no right to do
body: (осмеливаться, осмелиться; позволять себе, брать на себя смелость)
examples: I wouldn't presume to tell you how to run your own shop.
She presumed to speak for the whole department.
No one has ever presumed to question his figures.

entries.русский: полагать, предполагать; осмеливаться, осмелиться; позволять себе, брать на себя смелость

entries.meaning: To act as if something is true when it is not. ---
examples: Do not pretend you did not hear me.
He pretended to be asleep.
She is only pretending to be angry.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (pretend to be asleep), intransitive (children love to pretend)
entries.contrast: pretend to be something, or pretend that something is so.

entries.meaning: To decide which things matter most and deal with them first. ---
examples: You have to prioritize when the list gets long.
We prioritized the bugs that block users.
Safety is being prioritized over speed.
entries.русский: расставлять приоритеты, ставить на первое место
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (prioritize safety), intransitive (learn to prioritize)
entries.contrast: American prioritize; British prioritise.

entries.meaning: Realize has 3 distinct senses.
examples: I realize this is hard to hear.
She realized that her keys were still inside.
He had not realized how late it was.
It took twenty years to realize her dream of opening a bakery.
He never realized his full potential as a player.
The project has finally been realized, ten years after it was proposed.
They hope to realize a profit of two million dollars.
She realized three hundred thousand dollars on the sale of the house.
The fund has realized solid gains this year.

senses.head: To become aware of something you had not understood before
examples: I realize this is hard to hear.
She realized that her keys were still inside.
He had not realized how late it was.

senses.head: To make a hope, a plan, or an ability become real
examples: It took twenty years to realize her dream of opening a bakery.
He never realized his full potential as a player.
The project has finally been realized, ten years after it was proposed.

senses.head: To get a profit or an amount of money from a sale or an investment
examples: They hope to realize a profit of two million dollars.
She realized three hundred thousand dollars on the sale of the house.
The fund has realized solid gains this year.

entries.русский: осознавать, понимать; осуществлять, осуществить; реализовать (мечту, замысел); получать (прибыль), выручить; реализовать (актив)
entries.contrast: American realize; British realise.

entries.meaning: To think logically about something in order to reach a conclusion. ---
examples: Try to reason with her before you give up.
He reasoned that the store would still be open.
She is reasoning from a single example.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (he reasoned that it was safe), intransitive (reason with him)
entries.contrast: You reason with a person you hope to convince.

entries.meaning: Recall has 3 distinct senses.
examples: I cannot recall his last name.
She recalled the address perfectly.
He has recalled very little about that night.
If the part fails, the maker must recall it.
The company recalled forty thousand cars last spring.
Two brands of baby formula have been recalled.
Voters can recall a governor before the term ends.
They recalled two members of the school board.
The mayor was recalled in a special election.

senses.head: To bring something back into your mind, a little more formally than remember
examples: I cannot recall his last name.
She recalled the address perfectly.
He has recalled very little about that night.

senses.head: To order that a faulty product be returned by the people who bought it
examples: If the part fails, the maker must recall it.
The company recalled forty thousand cars last spring.
Two brands of baby formula have been recalled.

senses.head: To remove an elected official from office through a special vote
examples: Voters can recall a governor before the term ends.
They recalled two members of the school board.
The mayor was recalled in a special election.

entries.русский: вспоминать, припоминать; отзывать (товар), отозвать; изымать из продажи; отзывать (выборное лицо), смещать голосованием

entries.meaning: To think or suppose something, especially in informal speech. ---
examples: I reckon we can be there by noon.
He reckoned the trip would take six hours.
They are reckoning on a hundred guests.

entries.meaning: Recognize has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I did not recognize you with the beard.
She recognized his voice at once.
The state has recognized the marriage.
We want to recognize the people who made this possible.
The mayor recognized the firefighters at a ceremony downtown.
She has been recognized for thirty years of service.

senses.head: To know someone or something because you have met it before, or to admit that it is real
examples: I did not recognize you with the beard.
She recognized his voice at once.
The state has recognized the marriage.

senses.head: To give someone public credit or an award for what they have done
examples: We want to recognize the people who made this possible.
The mayor recognized the firefighters at a ceremony downtown.
She has been recognized for thirty years of service.

entries.русский: узнавать, признавать; отмечать, отметить (заслуги); награждать, чествовать
entries.contrast: American recognize; British recognise. The g is pronounced: REK-uhg-nyz.

entries.meaning: To think about a decision again and possibly change it. ---
examples: I hope you will reconsider.
The board reconsidered and voted again.
They are reconsidering the whole plan.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (reconsider the offer), intransitive (please reconsider)

entries.meaning: Reflect has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Take a week to reflect on the offer.
He reflected on how much had changed.
She is reflecting on twenty years of teaching.
Snow reflects most of the sunlight that hits it.
The mountains were reflected in the still lake.
The mirror was reflecting the light straight into my eyes.
These numbers reflect only the first quarter.
The results reflected months of hard work.
The change is already reflected in this month's bill.

senses.head: To think quietly and seriously about something
examples: Take a week to reflect on the offer.
He reflected on how much had changed.
She is reflecting on twenty years of teaching.

senses.head: To throw back light, heat, or an image from a surface
examples: Snow reflects most of the sunlight that hits it.
The mountains were reflected in the still lake.
The mirror was reflecting the light straight into my eyes.

senses.head: To show something clearly, or to be a sign of it
examples: These numbers reflect only the first quarter.
The results reflected months of hard work.
The change is already reflected in this month's bill.

entries.русский: размышлять; отражать; отражать, отразить (свет, изображение); отражать, показывать; свидетельствовать о
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (the price reflects demand), intransitive (reflect on the year)
entries.contrast: You reflect on a subject.

entries.meaning: Regard has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Many regard her as the best coach in the league.
He regarded the whole thing as a joke.
The book is widely regarded as a classic.
He regarded her in silence for a long moment.
The old cat regards every visitor with suspicion.
She stood in the doorway, regarding us coolly.

senses.head: To consider someone or something in a particular way
examples: Many regard her as the best coach in the league.
He regarded the whole thing as a joke.
The book is widely regarded as a classic.

senses.head: To look at someone or something steadily
examples: He regarded her in silence for a long moment.
The old cat regards every visitor with suspicion.
She stood in the doorway, regarding us coolly.

entries.русский: считать, расценивать; смотреть, разглядывать; пристально смотреть на
entries.contrast: regard someone as something, not regard someone like something.

entries.meaning: To feel sorry about something you did or failed to do. ---
examples: You will regret it if you skip the trip.
She regretted the email the moment she sent it.
He has always regretted leaving school early.
entries.contrast: The stress falls on the last syllable, so the t doubles: regretted, regretting.

entries.meaning: To depend on someone or something to work or to help. ---
examples: Small towns rely on volunteers.
We relied on his map and got lost.
She is relying on you to be there.
entries.contrast: Always rely on. The -y turns into -ies and -ied: relies, relied.

entries.meaning: To keep something in your mind or bring it back to mind. ---
examples: I remember the summer we spent there.
He remembered the password on the third try.
She is remembering it wrong.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (remember his name), intransitive (if I remember right)
entries.contrast: remember to do = не забыть сделать; remember doing = помнить, как делал.

entries.meaning: To study a subject carefully in order to find out new facts. ---
examples: Always research a company before the interview.
She researched the family tree for years.
He is researching rural schools in Ohio.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (research a topic), intransitive (research into the causes)
entries.contrast: The third person adds -es: researches.

entries.meaning: To settle a problem or an argument, or to decide firmly to do something. ---
examples: We need to resolve this before Friday.
They resolved the dispute out of court.
The issue has been resolved.

entries.meaning: Review has 3 distinct senses.
examples: Let us review the numbers one more time.
The committee reviewed all forty applications.
Your case is being reviewed.
She reviews restaurants for the local paper.
Critics reviewed the album kindly.
The book has been reviewed in every major paper.
I need to review chapter four before the quiz.
We reviewed the vocabulary all weekend.
She spent the night reviewing her notes.

senses.head: To look at something again in order to check or judge it
examples: Let us review the numbers one more time.
The committee reviewed all forty applications.
Your case is being reviewed.

senses.head: To give a public opinion in writing about a book, a movie, a restaurant, or a product
examples: She reviews restaurants for the local paper.
Critics reviewed the album kindly.
The book has been reviewed in every major paper.

senses.head: To go over material again in order to prepare for a test
examples: I need to review chapter four before the quiz.
We reviewed the vocabulary all weekend.
She spent the night reviewing her notes.

entries.русский: пересматривать, просматривать; рецензировать; писать отзыв (о книге, фильме); повторять (материал), готовиться (к экзамену)

entries.meaning: To change a text, a plan, or an opinion after thinking again. ---
examples: I need to revise the second paragraph.
They revised the budget twice.
The forecast has been revised downward.
entries.contrast: In American English revise means to change something; British students also use it for studying before an exam.

entries.meaning: To plan that something will happen at a particular time. ---
examples: Can we schedule the call for Tuesday?
They scheduled the surgery for April.
The flight is scheduled to land at noon.
entries.contrast: Americans say SKEJ-ool; the British say SHED-yool.

entries.meaning: To choose someone or something carefully from a group, a little more formally than choose. ---
examples: Select three photos for the front page.
The coach selected two new players.
She has been selected for the program.

entries.meaning: To feel or notice something without being told. ---
examples: Dogs sense fear.
I sensed that he wanted to leave.
She is sensing trouble ahead.

entries.meaning: To find the answer to a problem or a puzzle. ---
examples: Money alone will not solve this.
He solved the puzzle in four minutes.
The case was never solved.
entries.contrast: You solve a puzzle or an equation; you resolve an argument.

entries.meaning: To guess about something without having enough facts. ---
examples: I will not speculate about the cause.
Reporters speculated for days about her plans.
Everyone is speculating about who will get the job.
entries.contrast: You speculate about or on something.

entries.meaning: Spot has 3 distinct senses.
examples: See if you can spot the difference.
He spotted the error on page two.
She was spotted leaving the building.
Can you spot me twenty bucks until Friday?
He spotted me the cab fare.
She is always spotting her roommate lunch money.
Will you spot me on this set?
His friend spotted him while he benched.
Nobody was spotting her when the bar came down.

senses.head: To notice someone or something, often suddenly
examples: See if you can spot the difference.
He spotted the error on page two.
She was spotted leaving the building.

senses.head: To lend someone a small amount of money
examples: Can you spot me twenty bucks until Friday?
He spotted me the cab fare.
She is always spotting her roommate lunch money.

senses.head: To stand beside someone lifting weights, ready to take the bar if they cannot hold it
examples: Will you spot me on this set?
His friend spotted him while he benched.
Nobody was spotting her when the bar came down.

entries.русский: замечать, заметить; одолжить, подкинуть (немного денег); страховать (при подъёме штанги)
entries.contrast: One vowel plus one consonant, so the t doubles: spotted, spotting.

entries.meaning: To spend time learning about a subject, or to look at something closely. ---
examples: He wants to study engineering.
She studied the menu for five minutes.
They are studying for finals.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (study medicine), intransitive (study for a test)
entries.contrast: The -y turns into -ies and -ied: studies, studied, but studying keeps the y.

entries.meaning: To think that something is probably true. ---
examples: I suppose you are right.
Everyone supposed the meeting was canceled.
You are supposed to check in an hour early.
entries.contrast: be supposed to = должен, полагается: he is supposed to call.

entries.meaning: To think that something is probably true or that someone is probably guilty. ---
examples: I suspect she already knows.
Doctors suspected the flu at first.
He is suspected of taking the money.
entries.contrast: The verb is suh-SPEKT; the noun suspect is SUS-pekt.

entries.meaning: To believe that someone is honest or that something is safe. ---
examples: I trust him with the keys.
She trusted the directions and ended up lost.
He is trusted by everyone on the team.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (trust your doctor), intransitive (trust in the process)

entries.meaning: To check that something is true or accurate. ---
examples: Please verify the spelling of the name.
The bank verified my identity by phone.
The story has not been verified.
entries.contrast: The -y turns into -ies and -ied: verifies, verified.

entries.meaning: To form a clear picture of something in your mind. ---
examples: Try to visualize the finished room.
He visualized the jump before every attempt.
She is visualizing the route step by step.
entries.contrast: American visualize; British visualise.

entries.meaning: Weigh has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Weigh the costs against the benefits.
They weighed two offers before choosing.
Every option has been carefully weighed.
The package weighs about two pounds.
The nurse weighed the baby at every visit.
Have the bags been weighed yet?

senses.head: To think carefully about the good and bad sides of something
examples: Weigh the costs against the benefits.
They weighed two offers before choosing.
Every option has been carefully weighed.

senses.head: To have a particular weight, or to measure how heavy something is
examples: The package weighs about two pounds.
The nurse weighed the baby at every visit.
Have the bags been weighed yet?

entries.contrast: The gh is silent: WAY. The past is weighed, not weighted.
entries.phrasal verbs: weigh down · weigh in · weigh in · weigh on

entries.meaning: Wish has 2 distinct senses.
examples: I wish I had more time.
She wished him luck and left.
He is wishing for snow on his birthday.
Everyone stopped by to wish her luck.
He wished us a safe trip.
I have already wished him a happy birthday.

senses.head: To want something that is unlikely or impossible
examples: I wish I had more time.
She wished him luck and left.
He is wishing for snow on his birthday.

senses.head: To say that you hope someone will have something good
examples: Everyone stopped by to wish her luck.
He wished us a safe trip.
I have already wished him a happy birthday.

entries.transitivity: both — transitive (wish you luck), intransitive (wish for nothing)
entries.contrast: The third person adds -es: wishes. After wish use a past form: I wish I knew.

entries.meaning: To want to know something, or to ask yourself about it. ---
examples: I wonder what happened to them.
She wondered whether to say anything.
We were wondering if you could help.
entries.transitivity: both — transitive (I wonder what happened), intransitive (it makes you wonder)
entries.contrast: wonder WUN-dur = задаваться вопросом; wander WAHN-dur = бродить.

entries.meaning: Worry has 2 distinct senses.
examples: Do not worry about the test.
He worried all night about the results.
She has been worrying about money.
It worries me that she hasn't called.
The test results worried his doctor.
You're worrying your mother.

senses.head: To think about a problem in a way that makes you anxious
examples: Do not worry about the test.
He worried all night about the results.
She has been worrying about money.

senses.head: To make someone feel anxious
examples: It worries me that she hasn't called.
The test results worried his doctor.
You're worrying your mother.

entries.transitivity: both — transitive (it worries me), intransitive (do not worry)
entries.contrast: The -y turns into -ies and -ied: worries, worried. You worry about something.
